full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 filed the aforesaid suit praying for declaration of his title to the suit land on the basis of adverse possession alleging, inter alia, that one Satish Chandra Saha was the owner of .36 decimals of land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 318 and CS plot No. 426 of MouzaKhanpur 'Ma' Khanda under PS and District-Narayanganj. Similarly said Satish Chandra Saha was also the owner of .28 decimals of land of CS plot No. 425 of the same Khatian and mouza. Since most of the aforesaid land was diches and unused land said Satish Chandra Saha never enjoyed the same by taking physical possession thereof. The father of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 Kailash Chandra Singh took over possession of the suit land measuring .05 decimal to the north-east portion of CS plot No. 426 and developed the same and constructed two tin-shed huts by investing his own money and used to reside in one tin-shed with his family and the other hut was used by him as his grocery-Lakri shop since the middle of 1940. After about 2 months thereof the said Satish Chandra Saha found the father of plaintiff-opposite party No.1 in the suit land and asked him to vacate the same or he would take necessary action for evicting him by force therefrom. Inspite of such threat, the father of plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 continued in possession of the suit land within the knowledge of the said Satish Chandra Saha. Subsequently the father of the plaintiff-opposite party repaired his residential hut and extended his shop by investing more money and rented it out to various persons and received rent from them. In this way the father of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 enjoyed the possession of the suit land adversely against the said Salish Chandra Saha for more than 12 years since he took ever possession of the same in the middle of 1940 till he died in 1967 leaving behind plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 as his only heir. Thereafter the plaintif-opposite party No. 1 continued in possession of the suit land. Defendant No. 2 being the managing director of defendant No. 1, which is a commercial concern, held out a threat in February, 1988 to dispossess the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 disclosing that defendant No. 1 purchased the entire .64 decimals of land appertaining to plot Nos. 426 and 425 of the said mouza including the suit land by a sale deed in 1951 from to said Satish Chandra Saha. In this pack ground of the matter, plaintiff-oppositee party No. 1 was compelled to file the present suit for declaration of his title to the suit land on the basis of adverse possession.
